A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM4SVG. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references and supplementary material are readable, allowing retained, revised and relocated content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVG-generation comparisons in Table 2, embedding analyses, and a 37-participant user study in Table 3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the generation comparisons and user study, and adds original dataset analyses in Figure 2 and Section 5.1.

M1.justification: The method retains 55 SVG semantic tokens, description-based embedding initialization, optional image conditioning, and two-stage autoregressive instruction tuning. The expanded token catalog and revised architectural framing do not establish an implemented component change; both versions already describe initialization as averaging description embeddings.

E1.justification: SVGX-SFT names the existing corpus of approximately 250,000 SVGs and 580,000 instruction samples. The same generation and understanding tasks remain. The new dataset analysis and discussion of VGBench do not introduce another evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 2a removes the reproduced StarVector comparator reported in v1. The remaining quantitative and human-study comparator memberships are retained. The qualitative figure relabels LIVE as SD+LIVE while retaining its displayed outputs.

E3.justification: The reported learning rate changes from 2×10^-5 to 3×10^-4, and maximum sequence length increases from 2048 to 4096 tokens. These revise settings within the existing experiments; evaluation metrics and user-study procedures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 2 and Section 5.1 analyze vocabulary frequencies, SVG element counts before and after cleaning, and group-count distributions. The embedding visualization and primitive-ordering examples already appeared in v1; their relocation and annotation do not constitute new ablation experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same user-study averaging procedure and participant count. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new dataset-frequency plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds dataset statistics, removes the StarVector result row, replaces the displayed SVGDreamer examples, and removes three prompts from the main qualitative comparison. All retained numerical entries in Tables 2 and 3 match v1. The appendix comparison grid and final SVG gallery are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the averaging definition: v1 specifies n=55, whereas v3 defines n as the encoded description length. This resolves a mathematical inconsistency with the stated semantic-average initialization. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims the first framework supporting arbitrary LLMs/MLLMs, strengthening v1's pioneering-model framing. It recasts the architectural contribution as decoupling vector instructions and parameters and drops the explicit regression-head contribution. The central generation, understanding and dataset contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the dataset as predominantly UI-related and hierarchically structured. Appendix E adds explanations connecting primitive ordering to human drawing workflows, interpretability and usability. Future-work discussion expands to interactive refinement, cross-modal translation and domain adaptation; these are not evaluated capabilities.

D1.justification: Table S1 supplies the complete 55-token inventory and initialization descriptions, substantially expanding the central implementation specification. v3 also discloses two training epochs, cosine scheduling, 0.1 warmup, LlamaFactory and Unsloth, and annotates preprocessing steps. Conversely, it removes the dataset-source breakdown and the explicit LoRA rank and scaling values of 32.

R1.justification: A new vector-graphics-understanding subsection discusses YOLAT, YOLAT++ and VGBench and distinguishes their limitations from the proposed framework. v3 also adds LlamaFactory and Unsloth references and removes five dataset-source references. Most generation and LLM background remains.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the contribution list, portions of related work, implementation description, ablation discussion, conclusion and several appendix passages. It introduces a dataset-analysis subsection and reorganizes supplementary material around token specification, user evaluation and primitive ordering.

P2.justification: v3 adds a four-panel dataset figure and full-page token table, expands the architecture diagram, compresses Table 1, and rearranges the main comparison figure and tables. It relocates the primitive-ordering and embedding plots, annotates the embedding plot, and redraws the preprocessing diagram. Numerous captions are expanded.

improvement.justification: The corrected Equation 1, complete token descriptions and dataset analysis improve specification and understanding. However, v3 removes the reproduced StarVector comparison and dataset-source/LoRA details. It also changes reported training settings without explaining their relationship to the identical retained benchmark scores. These gains in specification and losses in empirical auditability leave the net quality direction uncertain.
